clue.text: A way artists have of laying it on thick

definitions.text: A way artists have of laying it on thick

parts.words: A way artists have of laying it on thick
parts.note: laying it on thick sounds like flattery, but here it is literal: a painting technique of applying paint in heavy, textured layers

explanation.surface: A remark that painters tend to exaggerate and flatter.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'laying it on thick' means overpraising; read literally it describes paint spread thickly enough to stand out from the canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the painting technique where pigment is applied so heavily that brush or knife marks stay visible.

clue.text: Maltreat a couple of students in one practice

indicators.note: in means the students go inside the other pieces

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
practice means use, as in custom
L is a learner or student, two of them here

explanation.surface: Two pupils are badly treated within one teaching practice.
explanation.walkthrough: L for a learner driver's plate stands for a student; 'in' puts LL inside I and USE.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone cruelly or abusively is a synonym for maltreat.

clue.text: Asian up in resort acccepts injection

indicators.note: accepts means the arranged letters take the jab inside them
resort, read as re-sort, says to rearrange the letters of up in

parts.note: an injection is a jab

explanation.surface: An Asian traveller at a holiday resort agrees to a vaccination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place, but read as 're-sort' it says to rearrange; 'accepts' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Punjab region of India and Pakistan is a person from Asia.

clue.text: Even crags could provide him with carrion to eat

indicators.note: could provide says the letters of the two words can be made into something new

explanation.surface: Rocky crags might supply a vulture with dead flesh to feed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could provide' rearranges EVEN CRAGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature that feeds on dead animals, like a hyena or vulture, is a scavenger by definition.

clue.text: Ecstatic state of a jumped-up cow?

explanation.surface: A question about the mood of a cow that jumped, as in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme 'Hey Diddle Diddle' the cow jumped over the moon; the phrase is also an idiom for delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrilled or delighted is expressed by this idiom; literally it is where the nursery-rhyme cow ended up.

clue.text: This is the Dominican friar's pigeon!

explanation.surface: An exclamation identifying the pet bird belonging to a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This is the' and the final 's link the two senses: the name was once given to Dominican friars in France (after their Paris church of St Jacques) and is also a breed of fancy pigeon with a hood of feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: French Dominicans were so called from their house of St Jacques in Paris, and a hooded breed of fancy domestic dove bears the same name.

clue.text: It may extinguish a fire in an aircraft

explanation.surface: Something that could put out flames on board a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong stream of water from a hose puts out flames; a jet-powered plane is also called by the same word.

clue.text: One arriving takes first right out of the resort

indicators.note: out of means the R is taken away from the resort's name

parts.note: Cromer is a seaside resort in Norfolk

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the first R of the resort's name, R standing for right

explanation.surface: A visitor makes a right turn to leave the seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromer is a Norfolk seaside town in England; 'takes' and 'out of' remove its first R.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer or someone who arrives, as in 'all comers', is called this.

clue.text: Bishop went on and delivered a reprimand

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess notation
went on means lasted, continued

explanation.surface: A bishop continued and then gave someone a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To blast is to criticise fiercely, so the past tense means scolded severely.

clue.text: Banknotes always in small numbers at present

indicators.note: in means the bundle and the always go inside

parts.note: nos is the short form of numbers
a wad is a bundle of banknotes
ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Cash in small denominations is always used these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small numbers' is the abbreviation NOS, not small digits; 'in' puts WAD and AY inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the present age or currently is a synonym of this adverb.

clue.text: Feature of cable laid by workers in a square

parts.note: a cable is a line, as in a telephone line

indicators.note: the workers are placed inside the letters for 'a square'

parts.note: T stands for a square, from the draughtsman's T-square
workers are men, as in the men on the shop floor

explanation.surface: A characteristic of electric wiring installed by labourers in a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MEN inside A and T; 'laid by' simply places the cable alongside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinctive facial feature or outline is called by this rather literary word, usually in the plural.

clue.text: Cry made initially by Macavity in an old warehouse

indicators.note: initially says to take the first letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: T. S. Eliot's mystery cat lets out a yowl inside a disused storehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Macavity is the criminal cat in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats, which keeps the cat-cry definition in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the sound a cat makes, a cry spelt out to imitate the noise.

clue.text: Notes removed by a dentist

explanation.surface: Written messages taken away by someone who treats teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A run of musical notes in order up or down makes a musical sequence; the hard tartar deposit a dentist scrapes off teeth has the same name.

clue.text: Allowed English class to be ordered about

indicators.note: about means the word for ordered goes around the other pieces

parts.note: ordered means told, as in told to do something
a class is a rate, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: An English school class was permitted to be bossed around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link and 'about' wraps the ordering word round the rest; 'class' tempts as a school group, but it means grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permitted or put up with without objection has been allowed, a near synonym.

clue.text: No bad doll he manufactured — look at it!

indicators.note: manufactured says the letters are made up into a new form

explanation.surface: A toymaker exclaims at the doll he has just made, which turned out fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges NO BAD DOLL HE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old exclamation calling attention to something surprising, like 'see here!'.

clue.text: How a one-armed bandit works without assistance?

explanation.surface: A question about how a slot machine operates, with a play on 'unaided'.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a slot machine with a lever; the first part reads the phrase literally, as if the bandit had only one hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a job on your own, with nobody helping, is the idiom; literally it is what someone with only one hand must do.

clue.text: It gets us over a dubious area, having nothing on the directors

definitions.text: It gets us over a dubious area

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket
the directors of a company are its board

explanation.surface: Something that helps us cross shaky ground, with nothing resting on the company's directors.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket; 'having' is a link. The definition is a walkway over muddy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A slatted wooden walkway laid over mud or wet ground lets people cross a boggy patch.

clue.text: Greyish-yellow ruler once in Castile

explanation.surface: A pale, sallow monarch from medieval Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The colour name is said to come from Queen Isabella of Castile, sponsor of Columbus.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale fawn shade takes this name, as did the Queen of Castile who sponsored Columbus's voyage.

clue.text: Marvellous musician with little resistance in extreme cold

definitions.text: with little resistance in extreme cold

parts.note: marvellous means super, as an exclamation of praise
a conductor is a musician who directs an orchestra

explanation.surface: A wonderful bandleader who copes poorly with very low temperatures.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a performer shivering on stage; the last half is really a description of a material science phenomenon.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain materials cooled near absolute zero carry electric current with virtually no opposition; such a substance has this name.

clue.text: Easter I associated with such a tranquil setting

definitions.text: Easter I associated with such a tranquil setting

parts.words: Easter I associated with such a tranquil setting
parts.note: Easter I is the abbreviation for Easter Island, which lies in an ocean whose name also means peaceful

explanation.surface: Easter Island evokes a calm, peaceful spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Easter I is Easter Island; 'tranquil' gives the adjective meaning peaceful, the sense behind the ocean's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means peaceable or calm, and it names the ocean in which Easter Island sits.

clue.text: Late deliveries? Exactly

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries
due means exactly, as in due north

explanation.surface: Delayed parcels? Precisely so.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled in succession, each one a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something past its expected time, such as a payment or a train, is late.

clue.text: Southern politician holding key to part of building

indicators.note: holding means the politician goes around the key

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A southern politician has the key to a section of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is the musical key E, not a door key.
explanation.definitionFit: One level or floor of a house or block is a part of building.

clue.text: Priestess given note before intonation in a church

indicators.note: before says the note comes first in the answer

parts.note: B is a musical note

indicators.note: in means the intonation sits inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
intonation is a chant, sung prayer

explanation.surface: A priestess receives a written message ahead of singing in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link; 'before' puts the note first, and 'in' sets the sung prayer inside the abbreviation for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A female follower or votary of Bacchus, the Roman god of wine, taking part in his rites.

clue.text: Heroine is the talk of the cavalry

definitions.text: Heroine is the talk of the cavalry

parts.words: Heroine is the talk of the cavalry
parts.note: the mounted soldiers' favourite subject is their steed, and the same word is slang for the drug heroin

explanation.surface: A celebrated woman is all the mounted regiment talks about.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter plays on heroin, whose slang name is the cavalry's animal; 'the Horse' is also a name for cavalry troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavalry soldiers ride and talk about their mounts, and the drug heroin has the same slang name.

clue.text: Part of the trouble a tragedian has making us cry

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the hardship a tragic actor goes through leaves the audience in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'has making us cry' is not a sense of the answer: only 'cry' defines it, with 'the', 'has making us' as surface links.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintive sound, especially of a sheep or goat, is a cry; also a whining complaint.

clue.text: Convict's poem accepted by the French king

indicators.note: accepted by means the poem goes inside the French word

parts.note: le is French for the
If is Kipling's famous poem
R stands for king, from the Latin rex

explanation.surface: A prisoner's verse was well received by the King of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking definition and wordplay; Kipling's 'If' is a staple short poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serving a life sentence is a convict known by this informal term.

clue.text: Bird found rings buried in untidy gardens

indicators.note: buried in means the rings go inside the jumbled letters
untidy says the letters of gardens are messed up

parts.note: rings look like the letter O, two of them here

explanation.surface: Some rings were discovered underground in messy flowerbeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' rearranges the garden letters to GSANDER, and 'buried in' puts the two rings inside it after the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A large diving duck with a serrated bill, found on rivers and lakes, is this bird.

clue.text: Pull up in narrow channel

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to pull is to tug

explanation.surface: Stopping in a narrow strait.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow passage of water, such as a strait, is called a gut.

clue.text: Pistol, possibly, of long ago

explanation.surface: A firearm, maybe an antique one.
explanation.walkthrough: Pistol is a swaggering soldier in Shakespeare's Henry plays, called Ancient Pistol: 'ancient' was an old word for an ensign, a junior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign was formerly given this rank title, as Shakespeare's Pistol was; it also means very old, belonging to times long past.

clue.text: Decrepit stranger in the outskirts of Derby

indicators.note: in places the comparative inside those two letters
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: stranger means odder, more peculiar

explanation.surface: A weak old outsider lives on the edge of the English city of Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is a city in the English Midlands; 'stranger' looks like a noun but is the comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shaky and infirm with age is said to totter, an informal adjective for frailty.
